note: The repertoire is small, so pieces recur on purpose: the Eight Great Pieces (三六, 欢乐歌, 行街, 中花六板/薰风曲, 慢六板, 四合如意, 云庆, 花三六/慢三六) heard from different ensembles. Built around the Lu Chunling, Zhou Hui, Zhou Hao and Ma Shenglong quartet (1983 China Record cassette), Shanghai conservatory and club groups (上海音乐学院教授丝竹研究组, 上海国乐研究社, Shanghai Traditional Music Society), a Shanghai teahouse ensemble, the Shanghai Chinese Orchestra's 1991 set of the eight pieces, and later readings (Guo Gan and Lingling Yu 2011, 华韵乐府 2015, 范临风 2024). 梵王宫 is another name of 阳八曲, and 薰风曲 of 中花六板. Release years are those of the edition read; the Naxos tracks carry 1992-93 dates and the 2002 Naxos ℗.

size.basis: Judgement made before collecting, not a count. The repertoire is small (the Eight Great Pieces plus a dozen or so other club pieces), but each piece has been recorded many times: by Shanghai amateur clubs, conservatory and state ensembles (Shanghai Conservatory, Zhejiang, Central Chinese Orchestra), China Record Company LPs and cassettes, Hong Kong and Taiwan labels (Hugo, ROI, Wind), and Western world-music labels (Ocora, Nimbus, Naxos, Smithsonian, Nonesuch). An insider's essential list is about 25 recordings: one or two good readings of each of the eight pieces plus Chunjiang huayue ye, Xing jie and a few club pieces.
